questions.stem: A service solves 5,000 LPs of about 900 variables each per night, one after another in one long-running process, on a machine with a GPU. Going by this lesson's measurements, where should they run?

options.text: On the CPU: each GPU solve costs about 0.2 s, the CPU takes milliseconds
options.says: Right: even the second GPU solve of a 100-variable LP took 0.21 s, while the CPU interior point solved 900 variables in 0.007 s.

options.text: On the GPU: once CUDA has started, each further solve is nearly free
options.says: After CUDA started, the same tiny LP still took 0.21 s on the GPU; the fixed cost is paid on every solve.

options.text: On the CPU, with PDLP, since it beats the interior point at that size
options.says: On the CPU, OR-Tools' PDLP is slower than the interior point at every size up to 300: 0.011 s against 0.007 s at 900 variables.

options.text: Split between both, since the devices are about equally fast at that size
options.says: At 900 variables the CPU took 0.007 s and neither GPU solver less than 0.18 s.

origin.section: Small LPs Lose to Start-Up and Fixed Costs

questions.stem: A report says cuOpt's PDLP solved a million-variable LP twice as fast as HiGHS's GPU PDLP, both run at their default settings. What must be weighed before calling cuOpt the faster solver?

options.text: cuOpt's time includes CUDA start-up, and HiGHS's time leaves it out
options.says: It is the other way round: cuOpt's column is its own solve time, which leaves out its process start and imports.

options.text: cuOpt ran on the CPU in that run, while HiGHS's PDLP ran on the GPU
options.says: Both are GPU solvers in the comparison; cuOpt's PDLP ran on the card too.

options.text: cuOpt stops at 1e-4 relative, and HiGHS's PDLP runs on to 1e-7
options.says: Right: cuOpt landed about 3e-5 from the optimum and HiGHS within 2e-9, so part of cuOpt's lead is accuracy it did not buy.

options.text: HiGHS's model held 4 million nonzeros, cuOpt's held 2 million
options.says: The program builds each LP once and hands the same numbers to every solver: a million variables, two million nonzeros.

questions.stem: A colleague says the GPU results only show that PDLP is a faster algorithm than interior point, whatever it runs on. What does the table's OR-Tools PDLP (CPU) column show?

options.text: On the CPU it beat interior point at every size, so the card adds little
options.says: On the CPU it was slower than interior point at 900, 10,000 and 90,000 variables.

options.text: On the CPU it lost to interior point up to 90,000 variables, so the card matters
options.says: Right: PDLP pays off when its matrix-vector products run on the GPU; on the CPU it only edged ahead at a million variables.

options.text: On the CPU it did not converge at a million variables, so only the card could
options.says: It converged at a million variables in 640 iterations, within 5e-9 of the interior point objective.

options.text: On the CPU it matched the GPU times, so the method alone explains the gain
options.says: At a million variables it took 11.1 s against 2.4 s for HiGHS's GPU PDLP.

origin.section: On the Build Machine's GPU, the Large LPs Are Where It Pays
